capabilities: create structured records inside a single plain-text note
view records as filtered tables, kanban boards, gallery cards, or slides
combine filter and sort rules into saved views
import text blocks and CSV files as records via a mapping wizard
export records to CSV for spreadsheet software
disambiguation: Not a Markdown table formatter or spreadsheet editor; it stores records as plain text in a note and renders them as database-style views.
extras: Desktop-only. The README emphasizes safety: the plugin only processes the file open in its view, data stays in the .md file so notes remain standard Markdown if uninstalled, and built-in auto-backup keeps file snapshot history. Points to the Obsidian Forum thread and GitHub issues for support; a related project, Foliole (an incremental reading app), is mentioned but separate.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to keep structured records and their table, board, gallery and slide views inside a regular note without frontmatter or code markup.

relations.evidence: AG Grid for the core table interaction model.

summary: Plain-text database plugin that builds Table, Kanban, Gallery and Slide views over structured records embedded directly in Markdown notes, without frontmatter.
